sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Container build and start steps
sections.what: Builds the AI service image in order: installs libraries, downloads the embedding model, copies the app, sets a non-admin user, and starts the server on port 8000.
sections.why: Likely reason: a repeatable package for running the service anywhere. The reason for the model download is stated in a comment.
sections.watch_out: The model download happens during the build, so changing the model name requires rebuilding the image.

summary: Build recipe that packages the AI service and its libraries, with an embedding model downloaded into the image, and runs it as a non-admin user.
purpose: Lets the AI service run the same way on any machine that can run containers.
why: Likely reason: downloading the embedding model at build time means the service does not need internet access when it starts. A comment in the file states this step.
how: First it starts from a slim Python 3.12 image and sets the working folder. It installs the listed Python libraries. It sets model cache folders and downloads the embedding model into the image. It copies the app code, creates a non-root user, gives that user the folder, and starts the server with two worker processes on port 8000.
inputs: The requirements file and the app folder. Internet access during the build to download packages and the model.
outputs: A container image that starts the FastAPI server.
risks: Building needs internet access, and a failed model download breaks the build. The image is large because of the machine learning libraries. Each worker loads its own copy of the model, which uses extra memory.
debug: If the build fails at the model step, check network access and the model name. If startup runs out of memory, reduce the worker count. If the app is missing, check that the app folder was copied.
